why: One file object labelled Report sits inside a single laptop on the plain light field; nothing else exists yet.
The laptop's drive fails; the report fades to an empty outline and nothing on the field can bring it back.
The empty outline is labelled single point of failure, then 3-2-1 is set large beside it.
Four failures arrive one at a time around the single report, each a small labelled mark that lands on its word and empties the file.
The report copies twice into three files in a row; one is struck and two remain. The 3 lights.
A copy moves from the laptop to an external drive; a fault strikes the laptop only and the drive's copy stays whole. The 2 lights.
A boundary draws round the desk holding laptop and drive; one event fills the whole boundary and both copies go together.
A copy travels out of the boundary to a cloud far across the field, out of the event's reach. The 1 lights.
A lock spreads along a connected line into one backup; the disconnected copy, with no line to it, stays clean.
The whole system at rest: laptop, external drive and cloud, each holding its copy, with 3, 2 and 1 lit beside them.
A bag outline holds a laptop and a USB drive, each with a copy of the report; 3, 2 and 1 sit below, unlit, waiting.
3 and 2 light, 1 stays dark and is marked missing; then the bag leaves the field with both copies inside.
The opening laptop fails again exactly as before; the report comes back from the external drive while the cloud copy stays whole.
Three file objects, each beside the 3-2-1 marks, waiting to be checked off: the viewer's own task.

The allocation makes b01 a presenter bookend because the request sets avatar.provider 'presenter' (loom/allocate.py: avatar_on unless provider is 'none'); the request's notes and the brief ask for no presenter. The storyboard gate refuses a bespoke kind against the allocation, so the presenter stays as the option and the motion-graphics version is the ready alternative: a person switches with `py -m loom switch <id> b01 "motion graphics, no presenter"` or sets the request's avatar provider to none.
